title: SOC Log Triage, SIEM Alerting & Anomaly Detection
summary: Interpret Apache/Nginx/Auth logs, correlate suspicious IOC signatures, and eliminate blind spots from sensitive credential logging.
learningObjectives: Spot automated credential stuffing, directory traversal, and SQLi probes directly inside access logs
Write structured tamper-evident audit trails without accidentally logging passwords or JWT tokens

sections.heading: 1. Reading Signals Inside High-Volume Telemetry
sections.content: A Security Operations Center (SOC) relies on centralized immutable logs ingested into a SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system. Analysts look for correlation indicators of compromise (IOCs): bursts of `HTTP 401/403` against `/login` from single IPs (credential stuffing), sudden `404` scans targeting `/wp-admin` or `/.env` (reconnaissance), URL payloads encoding `UNION SELECT` or `../etc/passwd`, and atypical off-hour admin token usage from new ASNs.

codeExamples.code:
[Firewall/Proxy/App Auth Logs] ---> [Centralized Immutable SIEM (Splunk/ELK/Datadog)]
                                        | Correlation Rule: >20 HTTP 401 in 60s
                                        v
                                 [High-Severity Alert -> Analyst Triage -> WAF Block]
codeExamples.explanation: Centralized correlation turns isolated raw requests into prioritized actionable incidents.

keyPoints: NEVER log plaintext passwords, API bearer secrets, or session tokens into application stdout logs!
Ship logs continuously offsite so an attacker obtaining local root cannot erase their entry trail cleanly.
commonMistakes: Logging entire raw HTTP `headers` objects during errors, accidentally persisting `Authorization: Bearer ...` secrets to Splunk/CloudWatch.

sections.heading: 2. Practical Log Parsing & IOC Extraction
sections.content: Analysts run repeatable log-filtering pipelines to summarize offending source IPs and distinguish benign 404 typos from targeted exploits.

codeExamples.code:
# Identify top IPs triggering HTTP 401 brute-force probes on /api/login
grep "POST /api/login HTTP" /var/log/nginx/access.log | awk '$9 == 401 {print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 5

# Detect directory traversal or SQLi query tampering probes
grep -E "(\.\./|UNION(%20|\+)SELECT|/\.env)" /var/log/nginx/access.log
codeExamples.explanation: Sorting and frequency-counting HTTP 401 actors highlights automated brute-force scanners instantaneously.
codeExamples.expectedOutput:
482 203.0.113.45
    19 198.51.100.14
Matched exploit signatures referencing /api/search?q=1' UNION SELECT...

keyPoints: Include UTC ISO-8601 timestamps, correlation Request IDs, and actor IDs in every structured JSON security log.
commonMistakes: Storing logs solely in rotating local `/tmp` buffers that vanish on server restarts.

exercises.title: Analyze Raw Server Logs & Triage Attack Vector
exercises.objective: Extract attacker IP, target route, and classify threat pattern cleanly.
exercises.description: Inspect 4 sample Apache log entries: 3 rapid POSTs returning 401 from `198.51.100.77` followed by `GET /api/courses?q=x' OR 1=1-- 500` from the same IP.
exercises.starterCode:
# Log Triage Worksheet
Attacker IP: ...
Tactic 1 (Repeated 401s): ...
Tactic 2 (OR 1=1--): ...
Immediate Mitigation: ...
hints: The repeated 401 failures indicate credential stuffing / brute forcing; `' OR 1=1--` indicates SQL injection probing.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Source `198.51.100.77` executes credential stuffing followed by SQL injection; block the IP at WAF/firewall and confirm `/api/courses` uses parameterized bindings.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why must authentication middleware strip `Authorization` headers and password fields before emitting error logs?

options.text: Logging credentials plaintext turns log aggregation tools into exposed breach targets if internal log viewers lack strict access limits
HttpOnly cookies fail if strings print to console

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Secret redaction guarantees sensitive tokens never accumulate silently in monitoring backends.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What threat does `GET /download?file=../../../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1` represent in proxy logs?

options.text: Path Traversal / Local File Inclusion attempt

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Relative parent sequences (`../`) attempt to break out of the intended folder root.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why should logs stream immediately off host servers into append-only central storage?

options.text: To preserve tamper-evident forensics even if a local host is compromised and local `/var/log` is altered
To shrink PostgreSQL CPU load directly
Because local disks refuse plaintext writes
To speed up CSS rendering in browsers

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Remote immutable shipping denies attackers the ability to scrub traces cleanly post-intrusion.

recap: You practiced high-signal SOC log parsing, IOC classification, and secret-safe structured audit logging.
